criteria.evidence: Ran a malformed-payload sweep against every write endpoint via fastapi.testclient. 13 of ~20 cases returned 500 with body 'Internal Server Error' and Content-Type text/plain (empty object, explicit nulls, wrong field types, syntactically broken JSON, truncated body, no body, quantity as a non-numeric string, 1e309, NaN); server-side traceback captured: app.py:55 'quantity = int(body["quantity"])' -> KeyError: 'quantity'. Worse, invalid input was also ACCEPTED with 200: quantity=-1 stored as -1; a 5,000,000-character name stored whole; Content-Type text/plain accepted as JSON; an 800-level nested array stored as the value of the 'name' string field; a NUL byte and an RTL-override character stored unfiltered. There is no error envelope at all -- the only structured 4xx observed came from FastAPI's own path-param coercion ('/items/abc' -> 422), so shapes are inconsistent across the surface. Injection/template probes (SQL fragments, {{7*7}}, ${7*7}, ../../etc/passwd) were stored and echoed inertly with no evaluation -- the one sub-case that passed.

Not executable as specified, and fails on the executable substitute. grep for psycopg/asyncpg/sqlalchemy/postgres/DATABASE_URL across app.py and test_app.py returned zero matches: there is no database, no connection pool, and no timeout to configure, so 'stop the DB', 'kill a connection mid-request', and 'recover without a restart' cannot be run. State lives in module-global dicts (users_db, items_db, next_item_id). Executed substitute: destroying the backing store at runtime made GET /items return 500 'Internal Server Error' (unstructured, text/plain) while /health kept returning 200 {'status':'ok'}; reloading the module (process-restart analog) left 0 of 100 previously written rows. 100 concurrent creates all returned 200 with 0 lost writes -- the only sub-case that passed.

Total authentication compromise, executed. Tokens are minted as 'tok-<username>' by POST /login, which never checks the password, and get_current_user accepts ANY string beginning with 'tok' and derives identity by string-stripping it. Sending 'Authorization: Bearer tok-bob' from an unauthenticated client returned 200 with bob's record. Every invalid-credential case returned 500, not 401: no header (KeyError on request.headers['authorization']), 'Bearer' with no value, a random token, and a token in the query string. A token for a never-registered user ('tok-ghostuser') returned 200. Cross-user authorization: as alice, GET /items/1 returned bob's item in full ({'name':'bobs-private-item','owner':'bob'}), and DELETE /items/1 returned {'success': true} and actually destroyed it -- no handler compares current_user to the resource owner anywhere in app.py. Mass-assignment of 'owner' was ignored (the one sub-case that passed).

No schema exists. There are no migrations, no DDL, no SQL files and no database driver in the submission, so 'migrations run against an empty database' could not be executed; there are consequently zero tables, zero foreign keys, zero ON DELETE behaviours, zero DB-level constraints, and no timestamptz (no timestamps at all). Credential leakage confirmed by response capture: POST /register with password 'hunter2' returned {'username':'carol','password_hash':'sha256$2retnuh'} and GET /me returned the same -- and the 'hash' is the plaintext password reversed (app.py:32, password[::-1]), so this is plaintext credential disclosure with a label on it, not a hash. Pagination absent: after inserting 500 rows, GET /items returned all 501 rows in one unbounded body; the handler is 'return list(items_db.values())' with no limit or offset parameters.

Executed the suite: 3 passed in 0.19s (test_health, test_register, test_login). All four required auth-boundary tests are missing -- there is no test sending no credential, no test sending a malformed credential, no test for an expired credential (the token format carries no expiry to test), and no test using a valid credential against another user's resource. The suite contains no assertion about status 401 or 403 anywhere. It also runs entirely against in-process module-global dicts, not a real Postgres, which the rubric fails independently.

No pipeline exists to run: there is no .github/ directory, no workflow YAML, no Dockerfile, no requirements/pyproject manifest, and the directory is not a git repository ('fatal: not a git repository'), so the criterion cannot be executed as written. Executed the strongest available substitute -- seeded four defects one at a time into a copy and ran the submitted suite. 3 of 4 went undetected: inverting the token guard so every valid token is rejected and every invalid one accepted -> 3 passed; removing quantity validation entirely -> 3 passed; deleting the authorization dependency from GET /items/{item_id} outright -> 3 passed. Only changing /register's success status 200 -> 201 went red ('assert 201 == 200'), and it caught a status code, not a security defect.

Could not be executed: there is no workflow file anywhere in the submission (find for *.yml/*.yaml returned nothing outside .pytest_cache), so there is nothing to inspect for checkout/install/lint/type-check/test steps, no Postgres service container, and no action versions or runtimes to check against the currently-supported set. There is also no lint or type-check configuration of any kind (no ruff, no mypy, no pyproject.toml).

Could not be executed as a deployment: no public URL, no container, no host configuration, and no process manager are present. The README's documented run command was executed literally -- 'python app.py' exited 0 in under a second having bound no port, because app.py contains no __main__ block and no uvicorn.run call, so the documented path never starts a service. Health honesty was executed in-process and fails: /health is 'return {"status": "ok"}' with no dependency check, and it returned 200 {'status':'ok'} unchanged while the backing store was destroyed and GET /items was simultaneously returning 500. A health check that cannot fail reports nothing.

Could not be executed: there is no Dockerfile, so no image can be built or inspected -- multi-stage build, USER directive, non-root runtime, and absence of build tooling in the runtime layer are all unverifiable and therefore unpassable. There is no git repository, so git log -p and git log --all --full-history could not be run for committed credentials. There is no .gitignore in the submission and no .env handling: grep for os.environ/getenv/DATABASE_URL across the source returned zero matches, so no configuration comes from the environment. Separately, the reversible password encoding at app.py:32 is a credential-handling defect regardless of packaging.

Followed the 10-line README literally from the target directory. Its only instruction, 'python app.py', executed and exited 0 with no output and no listening socket -- a documented command that does not do what it documents. The README does not cover local setup, how to run the tests, the schema, the auth model, or the error envelope; a stranger could not run the test suite from it (the actual invocation requires installing fastapi/httpx/pytest, which the README never mentions and no manifest declares). Logs: grep for logging/logger across the source returned zero matches -- the application emits no log lines at all, so there is nothing structured, no correlation id, and no log levels; the only output produced during the failure scenarios was an uncaught Python traceback on stderr. No portfolio write-up exists in the submission (the directory contains exactly app.py, test_app.py, README.md).

verdicts.highest_leverage_gap: The bearer token is an unsigned, self-asserting string of the form tok-<username> that /login issues without checking the password and that no handler ever compares against a resource owner, so any caller can mint any user's identity and read or delete their data -- nothing else is worth fixing until credentials are unforgeable and ownership is checked on every access.
